text_blocks.snippet: PR immigration refers to Permanent Resident immigration, where an individual gains the legal right to reside permanently in a country they are not a citizen of. This status, often granted through a "green card" (in the US) or similar documentation (like a PR card in Canada), allows the individual to live, work, and sometimes study in the country, but typically does not include the full rights of a citizen, such as voting.
snippet_highlighted_words: Permanent Resident immigration, where an individual gains the legal right to reside permanently in a country they are not a citizen of

list.title: Permanent Resident Status:
list.snippet: This is a legal status granted to foreign nationals, allowing them to live and work in a country permanently, though they remain citizens of another country.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: In the US, permanent residents are often referred to as "green card holders". In Canada, they have a "Permanent Resident card".

list.title: Rights and Responsibilities:
list.snippet: While permanent residents have many rights similar to citizens (e.g., the right to work, live in the country), they may not have the right to vote, hold certain public offices, or access some social benefits that are reserved for citizens.

list.title: How to Obtain:
list.snippet: Permanent residency can be obtained through various pathways, including family sponsorship, employment, or specific categories like refugees or victims of certain crimes.

list.title: Travel:
list.snippet: Permanent residents can travel outside the country, but usually need to carry their permanent resident card or a similar travel document for re-entry.

list.title: Citizenship:
list.snippet: Permanent residency is a step towards citizenship, but it's not the same thing. Many countries have a separate process for naturalization, where permanent residents can apply to become citizens after meeting specific requirements.

text_blocks.snippet: A "permanent resident" and a "green card" are essentially the same thing in the context of U.S. immigration. The "green card" is the common term for the Permanent Resident Card (Form I-551), which is the document that proves a foreign national has been granted lawful permanent resident status in the United States.

list.title: Green Card (Permanent Resident Card):

list.title: Interchangeable Terms:

list.title: Purpose of the Card:
list.snippet: The green card allows the holder to live and work anywhere in the U.S. permanently, and it also serves as a valid form of identification.

list.title: Renewal:
